findings.title: Restore decision depends on key window state at completion time
findings.message: The restore check runs in the completion handler, after AppKit has typically already dismissed the sheet/panel and moved key status. At that point NSApp.keyWindow is often the parent or nil, so the heuristic is unreliable. When the panel is app-modal (not a sheet), key may be the panel only transiently. The result is that restoration may be skipped when needed, or applied in unintended states.
findings.suggestion: Capture whether the panel owned focus at a deterministic time, or verify behavior on a real window, and document or test the ordering. Consider restoring only when key is nil or the parent.

findings.title: Test covers only predicate, not restoration behavior
findings.message: The fixture only tests a pure predicate with dummy NSObjects. It does not exercise the completion handler, the weak parent capture, the orderOut/makeKeyAndOrderFront calls, or the first-responder restore. The test name overstates what it verifies, and regressions in the real wiring would go undetected.
findings.suggestion: Rename the test to reflect predicate coverage, or add an integration test that drives a real NSWindow with a panel.
